discovery.tab_hint_solutions: Generate possible solutions without committing to any. Quantity before quality — diverge first, converge later.

discovery.tab_hint_metrics: Define how you will know if the solution generated real value. Establish baseline and target before building.
discovery.tab_hint_project_charter: Formalize the executive scope of the initiative. Register purpose, objectives, deliverables, constraints, sponsor and owner to turn Discovery into structured execution.

RICE.label: RICE
RICE.summary: Prioritize based on reach, impact, confidence, and effort. It is best suited to compare product opportunities with a focus on relative impact.
RICE.bullet1: Reach estimates how many users or accounts will be affected.
RICE.bullet2: Impact and Confidence help weight perceived value and certainty of the hypothesis.
RICE.bullet3: Effort lowers priority for items that are expensive or slow to deliver.

ICE.label: ICE
ICE.summary: ICE simplifies the analysis using impact, confidence, and ease. It is useful when you want a quick prioritization without depending on a detailed reach estimate.
ICE.bullet1: Simpler and faster than RICE for initial triage.
ICE.bullet2: Helps order hypotheses when reach is still unclear.
ICE.bullet3: Works well in discovery and early backlog shaping.

MOSCOW.label: MoSCoW
MOSCOW.summary: MoSCoW classifies the item by criticality: must have, should have, could have, or won't have now. It is ideal for scope negotiation and expectation alignment.
MOSCOW.bullet1: Must Have represents items essential to the objective.
MOSCOW.bullet2: Should Have and Could Have help organize incremental scope.
MOSCOW.bullet3: Won't Have makes explicit what stays out of this cycle.

EISENHOWER.label: Eisenhower
EISENHOWER.summary: The Eisenhower Matrix organizes work by urgency and importance. It complements the other methods when you need to quickly decide what should be done now, planned, delegated or dropped.
EISENHOWER.bullet1: Important and urgent: do it now.
EISENHOWER.bullet2: Important and not urgent: schedule it.
EISENHOWER.bullet3: Urgent but not important or neither urgent nor important: delegate, postpone or discard.

WSJF.label: WSJF
WSJF.summary: Weighted Shortest Job First prioritizes by dividing cost of delay by job size. It is best suited to rank user stories and enablers using economic impact and timing.
WSJF.bullet1: Combines business value, time criticality and risk reduction.
WSJF.bullet2: Divides cost of delay by job size to highlight the best economic sequencing.
WSJF.bullet3: Works best for backlog user stories and enablers.

requirements.type_desc_BUSINESS: BR — Business Rule: rule imposed by the business, independent of technology. e.g. calculation formula, eligibility criteria.
requirements.type_desc_FUNCTIONAL: FR — Functional: what the system must do. e.g. the user can filter by date range.
requirements.type_desc_NON_FUNCTIONAL: NFR — Non-Functional: how the system must perform. e.g. response time < 2s, 99.9% uptime.
requirements.type_desc_DATA: DR — Data: data structure, format, retention or quality. e.g. date must be ISO 8601.
requirements.type_desc_INTEGRATION: IR — Integration: how the system connects to external APIs or services. e.g. sync with Azure DevOps.
requirements.type_desc_SECURITY: SR — Security: authentication, authorization, encryption, audit. e.g. data at rest AES-256.
requirements.type_desc_COMPLIANCE: CR — Compliance: legal, regulatory or contractual obligation. e.g. LGPD, SOX, Cisco Partner Agreement.
requirements.type_desc_UX: UXR — UX/Usability: interface and experience requirements. e.g. accessible via keyboard, WCAG AA.
